name: lotse
description: Lotse — an ACP client. Starts coding agents as subprocesses over the Agent Client Protocol, manages their sessions, and binds them to a surface. Runs on GJS via gjsify.

description.p: Lotse is a client for the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), the open standard a coding agent speaks over a JSON-RPC connection on stdio. It starts the agent as a subprocess, keeps its session, and shows you what the agent says while it works.
description.translatorHint: Opening paragraph: what the app is and which standard it speaks

description.p: The agent decides which model does the work; lotse owns the environment around it — which directory the session runs in, what the agent is allowed to do, and which MCP servers it may reach. A session record says what is reachable, never what is allowed, so every request is checked again, every time.
description.translatorHint: Second paragraph: the app's own scope versus the agent's

ul.item: Start, list, resume and cancel agent sessions, from the command line or from a window
ul.translatorHint: Feature list: the session commands

ul.item: Watch one prompt turn stream in, and stop it without killing the session
ul.translatorHint: Feature list: streaming a turn and stopping it

ul.item: Answer the agent's permission requests yourself — lotse denies by default rather than approving for you
ul.translatorHint: Feature list: the permission gate

ul.item: One agent needs no driver: opencode today, anything that speaks ACP tomorrow
ul.translatorHint: Feature list: the protocol means no per-agent driver

description.translatorHint: Bullet list of what the app does

description.p: Lotse can download its OpenCode for you when none is installed.
description.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.5.0 - opening line: Lotse can download its own OpenCode

ul.item: lotse agents --install downloads the pinned OpenCode for your user after asking, and checks it before it is used.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.5.0 - agent install from the command line. Keep the command as it is.

ul.item: Apps that embed lotse can offer the same download without bundling the agent.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.5.0 - embedding apps can offer the install

description.p: Lotse speaks German, starts the bundled OpenCode by default and warns when a free model is in use.
description.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.4.0 - opening line: German translation, bundled OpenCode default, free-model warning

ul.item: The app, the widget, the command line and the notifications are translated into German.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.4.0 - German translation

ul.item: The bundled OpenCode, with its own login and settings, is the default agent. Your own OpenCode is an opt-in.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.4.0 - bundled OpenCode is the default agent

ul.item: A card above the message field warns while a free model is in use, because its provider may store and train on what you send.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.4.0 - warning while a free model is in use

ul.item: A running task can ask for you when only you can go on, for example for a login or a code.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.4.0 - a task can ask for the person

ul.item: A scheduled task that never ran now starts at its first matching time.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.4.0 - fix for scheduled tasks

description.p: Kurier is now lotse, and its building blocks are on npm for other apps to embed.
description.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.3.0 - opening line: the rename to lotse, the libraries on npm. Keep "Kurier" and "lotse" as they are.

ul.item: The libraries @lotse/acp, @lotse/session, @lotse/core and @lotse/widget are published on npm, so other apps can embed lotse.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.3.0 - the libraries are on npm. Keep the package names as they are.

ul.item: Local models and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint can be added as a provider for the bundled OpenCode.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.3.0 - custom and local model providers

ul.item: Provider settings in Preferences: connect or log out of providers and manage your own.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.3.0 - provider settings page in Preferences

ul.item: Questions from scheduled tasks can be answered from a notification or an answer window.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.3.0 - answering a lotse serve question from the desktop

ul.item: Tool calls are stored in the conversation with their details, and a host can show its own tools with its own title and icon.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.3.0 - structured tool calls in the transcript

ul.item: A host app can limit which models a chat may use.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.3.0 - host model policy

ul.item: The login now offers xAI (Grok).
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.3.0 - xAI added to the login

ul.item: A host app can run a single prompt as a headless job, with no chat window, and get a typed result back.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.3.0 - headless jobs (runJob)

ul.item: Kurier is now called lotse. An installed Kurier is upgraded, and your sessions and settings are moved over once.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.3.0 - the rename from Kurier to lotse. Keep "Kurier" and "lotse" as they are.

description.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.3.0 - the list of what changed

description.p: The first release with installable packages. Kurier can now log you in to your model providers itself, and the Flatpak brings its own copy of OpenCode.
description.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.1 - opening line: packages exist now, login from the app, bundled OpenCode in the Flatpak. Keep "OpenCode" and "Flatpak" as they are.

ul.item: Log in to a model provider from Kurier, with a browser sign-in or an API key, for every provider the agent offers. No terminal needed.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.1 - logging in to providers from the app, by browser sign-in or API key

ul.item: The Flatpak includes OpenCode, which runs with its own settings and login, separate from any OpenCode already on your computer, and has network access to reach its provider.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.1 - the Flatpak bundles OpenCode with its own home directory and network access. Keep "OpenCode" and "Flatpak" as they are.

ul.item: A clearer message when your account has no credit left, instead of a message that looks like a failed login.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.1 - a distinct message for an account without credit

ul.item: Fixes for Windows and macOS: agents installed as command shims are found, and the agent's working directory is handled correctly.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.1 - Windows and macOS fixes

ul.item: Packages for Debian and Ubuntu (.deb), Fedora (.rpm), AppImage, macOS, Windows and Flatpak. They are not signed yet.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.1 - the package formats now offered, with an honest note that they are unsigned. Keep the file extensions and format names as they are.

description.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.1 - the list of what changed

description.p: The first release of Kurier, a desktop client for the Agent Client Protocol — the open standard a coding agent speaks over. Kurier starts an agent such as OpenCode as a program on your own computer, keeps the conversation, and shows you what the agent says while it works. The agent and the model behind it are not part of Kurier: you install and log in to those yourself.
description.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.0 - what Kurier is, and that the agent is a separate program the user installs

description.p: This first version does the following:
description.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.0 - lead-in to the list of what the first version does

ul.item: A list of your sessions on the left, so you can pick up an earlier conversation instead of starting over.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.0 - the session list

ul.item: One real turn with the agent: the answer arrives piece by piece while the agent works, and Stop ends the turn without closing the session.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.0 - a real agent turn, streaming and Stop. Keep "Stop" as it is, it is a button name.

ul.item: When the agent asks permission to do something, a dialog asks you, and you can allow it once or refuse it. There is deliberately no "always allow" button: a permission nobody sees again is a permission nobody revoked.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.0 - the allow-once permission dialog. Keep "always allow" as it is, it names a button that is absent.

ul.item: A layout that fits a phone as well as a desktop, down to a window width of 360 pixels.
ul.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.0 - the phone-width layout. Keep "360" as it is.

description.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.0 - the list of what the first version does

description.p: Not in this release: several agents side by side, a web version, and a Telegram bot. The command line client is here already. And the Flatpak is an installer rather than a sandbox — an agent has to run on your computer, so Kurier asks for access to your files and to the session bus.
description.translatorHint: Release notes for version 0.1.0 - what is not there yet, plus an honest note that the Flatpak grants broad access
